metadata.title: D'Andre Swift (hip/knee) doesn't practice Wednesday
metadata.description: D'Andre Swift (hip/knee) did not take part in Chicago's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Swift is currently dealing with a couple of different injuries. The team held him out of Wednesday's practice as a result. but it doesn't seem like he's at real risk of being sidelined in Week 5. Still, it would be worth it for fantasy managers to keep tabs on his status the rest of the week, especially with Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) also on the team's injury report.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift - DNP on Wednesday
metadata.description: Swift didn't practice Wednesday due to hip and knee injuries.
metadata.analysis: Both Swift and fellow RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) were non-participants to begin Week 5 prep, leaving question marks in the Bears backfield ahead of Sunday's contest at Green Bay. While Swift ceded 30 carries to Monangai in a Week 4 win against the Jets, the former notched 15 rushes and two catches en route to 74 yards from scrimmage. The overall situation will continue to be monitored to get a sense of who among the duo will be Chicago's lead runner this weekend.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift Misses Practice on Wednesday with Hip and Knee Issues
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (hip, knee) did not practice on Wednesday due to hip and knee injuries, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. Swift was listed on Chicago's injury report with the knee issue leading into Week 4, but the hip ailment appears to be a new injury. The 27-year-old has gotten off to a strong start to the 2026 season, recording 395 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns on 79 touches across four games. The severity of Swift's injuries is not yet clear, but his health is obviously worth monitoring for fantasy managers leading into the Bears' Week 5 matchup against the Green Bay Packers. Bears RB2 Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) also missed the team's practice on Wednesday due to thumb and toe injuries. If neither Monangai nor Swift can play against Green Bay, Chicago running back Roschon Johnson would likely be the next man up in the backfield.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift runs for 58 yards in Week 4 win
metadata.description: D'Andre Swift carried the ball 15 times for 58 yards while catching both of his targets for 16 yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4. He also lost a fumble in the win.
metadata.analysis: Swift spent some time on the sidelines after losing a fumble, although it is unclear whether he was benched or was dealing with an injury, as he got up slowly while favoring his knee after the play. Either way, he was outplayed by Kyle Monangai, who ran for 146 yards and two touchdowns. A low-end RB2 in fantasy moving forward, Swift will look to bounce back in Week 5 against the Packers.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift Fumbles and Loses Lead-Back Role in Week 4
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift rushed for 58 yards on 15 carries during Sunday's Week 4 win over the New York Jets. He also caught two passes for 16 receiving yards. Swift averaged fewer than four yards per carry, and he also fumbled the ball away for the second time in the last three weeks. Not only did the veteran have a suboptimal day, but his teammate, Kyle Monangai, was absolutely explosive. Monangai had one of the best games of his young career, carrying the ball 30 times for 146 rushing yards and two touchdowns. For Swift's fantasy managers, seeing his inefficiency, his fumble, and his teammate's career performance was a nightmare combination. This Chicago offense loves to run the football, so it's not as if Swift has lost his fantasy relevance forever. However, he entered this week as a top-eight running back in total scoring, and he'll leave this week as a low-end RB2 or high-end RB3 going forward. The good news for Swift is that he gets a softer matchup next week against the Packers.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift - Outplayed by Monangai in Week 4
metadata.description: Swift rushed 15 times for 58 yards and caught both of his targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 23-12 win over the Jets. He also lost a fumble.
metadata.analysis: Swift was stopped twice inside the 1-yard line on the opening drive, with the second stop resulting in a turnover on downs. Kyle Monangai got the goal-line opportunities on Chicago's next possession and punched in a one-yard touchdown. Swift also lost a fumble in the third quarter and watched Monangai dominate touches the rest of the way, as the latter finished with 146 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries. Both of Chicago's top two running backs are likely to play significant roles in Week 5 against Green Bay's shoddy run defense, assuming Monangai is able to play through the thumb injury he sustained during Sunday's win.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift (knee) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: D'Andre Swift (knee) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
metadata.analysis: Swift was held out of Chicago's practice on Thursday, but he returned to practice as a full participant on Friday and carries no injury designation heading into the weekend. He should be fully good to go for Sunday's game and should be a safe fantasy option against the Jets, though his fantasy upside will likely be limited with Caleb Williams (hamstring) out for another game.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift - Clear for Sunday
metadata.description: Swift (knee) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.
metadata.analysis: Swift didn't practice Thursday due to a knee injury, which coach Ben Johnson chalked up Friday to the running back "still feeling the effects" from Monday Night Football, per Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune. After an uncapped session to end Week 4 prep, Swift is in the clear for Sunday's contest, looking to resume the 20.7 touches per game that he's handled through three contests this season.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift (knee) expected to practice Friday
metadata.description: D'Andre Swift is expected to return to practice on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Swift was added to the injury report after not practicing on Thursday. Bears coach Ben Johnson said he is optimistic on Swift playing on Sunday.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift - Expected to practice Friday
metadata.description: Swift (knee) is expected to practice Friday, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reports.
metadata.analysis: Head coach Ben Johnson said Swift is still feeling the effects of Monday night's game after he was unable to practice Thursday. With Swift expected to take the field Friday, Johnson said he's optimistic the running back will be able to play Sunday against the Jets. Kyle Monangai could be in line to handle a bigger slice of the pie in the backfield on the short week.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift Has No Injury Designation for Week 4
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (knee) is off the final injury report after a brief scare Thursday. Swift was added to the report with the knee issue and did not practice, but Courtney Cronin of ESPN reported that he returned as a full participant Friday and has no game designation for Sunday's matchup with the New York Jets. Swift is coming off 20 carries for 84 yards in Monday night's win over Philadelphia, and he also caught two passes for four yards. He has 253 rushing yards and three touchdowns through three games. Kyle Monangai has stayed involved behind him, but Swift has led Chicago in carries every week so far. RotoBaller ranks him as RB15 for Week 4. Friday's full practice puts Swift back on track to handle his usual role Sunday.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift (knee) does not practice Thursday
metadata.description: D'Andre Swift (knee) was added to the injury for the Chicago Bears and did not practice Thursday according to Ari Meirov.
metadata.analysis: Swift's status will need to be monitored during Friday's practice session, as another missed opportunity could leave the running back's status in doubt, with Kyle Monangai in line for increased touches in Week 4 if Swift cannot suit up for head coach Ben Johnson.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift - DNP due to knee injury
metadata.description: Swift didn't participate in Thursday's practice due to a knee injury.
metadata.analysis: After the Bears held a walkthrough Wednesday, Swift wasn't included on the team's first Week 4 injury report, so his addition to it one day later could mean he sustained the issue on the practice field. In any case, his status now will be monitored closely to get a sense of his odds to suit up Sunday versus the Jets. If Swift isn't able to go or is at all inhibited, fellow RB Kyle Monangai could be in line for a significant boost in touches and snaps.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift Misses Practice on Thursday with Knee Injury
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (knee) did not participate in his team's practice on Thursday due to a knee injury. The 27-year-old was not listed on Wednesday's injury report, so it appears the knee issue is a new development. Swift has gotten off to a strong start to the 2026 season, recording 321 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns on 62 touches across three games. While the severity of his knee injury is not yet known, the veteran back could be in danger of missing Chicago's Week 4 contest against the New York Jets. If Swift is inactive this week, Bears running back Kyle Monangai would likely handle the majority of the team's backfield duties and would profile as a must-start running back for fantasy managers against the Jets.

metadata.title: Large Workload Fuels Big Start to Season for D'Andre Swift
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift continues to exceed expectations in his age-27 season. The veteran running back logged a season-high 22 touches last week, and he's now averaging 20.7 touches per game this year. Not only is he handling a large workload, but he has also been quite productive. Swift ranks as the overall RB7 in PPR leagues this year with 253 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns. He has been able to fend off any sort of competition from Kyle Monangai, who has 10 carries in all three games this year but has handled a moderately low snap share while having a smaller role in the receiving game. It was especially encouraging to see Swift have such a productive game in Week 3, despite Caleb Williams (hamstring) being sidelined. Regardless of who quarterbacks the Bears in Week 4 and beyond, Swift should remain a high-end RB2 in fantasy football.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift runs for 84 yards in Week 3
metadata.description: D'Andre Swift carried the ball 20 times for 84 yards and caught two of his three targets for four yards in a 27-7 win over the Eagles in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Swift led the way on the ground for the Bears, although he was held out of the end zone for the second straight game. Overall, the veteran running back has rushed for 253 yards and three touchdowns while adding eight catches for 68 yards in three games this season. He will be on the RB1 radar in fantasy in Week 4 against the Jets.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift - Strong finish in Week 3 win
metadata.description: Swift rushed 20 times for 84 yards and brought in two of three targets for four yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
metadata.analysis: Facing the team he suited up for back in 2023, Swift had a nifty nine-yard run on the Bears' opening possession, but he otherwise found running room at a premium for the next two-plus quarters. However, Swift got it going late to help ice Chicago's impressive win, rattling off 23 yards on the first three plays of the Bears' final drive and then closing things out with a 15-yard tackle-breaking scamper on fourth-and-1 on the first play after the two-minute warning. Swift has eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign and will take an average of 4.7 yards per carry into a Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift Loses Fantasy Appeal with QB Uncertainty
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift has a lower overall floor and ceiling in Monday night's home matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. The 27-year-old has been solid thus far in 2026, averaging nearly five yards per carry (4.97) on 34 totes across the first two contests. Unfortunately, quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) will miss time, dropping the offense's potency for now. On the bright side, Swift was heavily involved in the passing game during Week 2 (five for 54) and could see his overall volume tick up with either Tyson Bagent (concussion) or Case Keenum at the helm. Philadelphia's defense isn't enticing opposition, although they currently rank as a bottom-10 unit against the run, yielding 127 yards per game. The former Georgia Bulldog's value takes a hit in Week 3, but he's still a solid option at the position. Swift is RotoBaller's PPR RB22 ahead of Monday Night Football.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift Could See Larger Role Without Starting Quarterback
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift is off to a very good start to the 2026 season and that could continue as he could see an increased role in the offense with quarterback Caleb Williams expected to miss time with a hamstring injury. Swift came out of the gates this season rolling with an epic Week 1 performance against the Panthers when he rushed 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns with one catch for 10 yards. The going got tougher against the Vikings in Week 2, but he still carried the ball 16 times for just 45 rushing yards and caught five passes for 54 yards. Against the Eagles in Week 3, Swift should continue to be heavily involved maybe even more than the previous two weeks. While the Eagles could sell out to stop Swift and the run game without the threat of Williams and the passing attack, Swift could also use his increased role to have another good fantasy day.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift leads quiet offense in Week 2 loss to Vikings
metadata.description: D'Andre Swift rushed 16 times for 45 yards while also hauling in each of his five targets for a team-high 54 yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Swift continues a solid stretch out of the backfield to begin the season, finishing with over 90 offensive yards in each of the first two games. The running back will look to remain one of the more impactful options in the Chicago offense as the season moves on, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift - Falls just short of 100 scrimmage yards
metadata.description: Swift carried the ball 16 times for 45 yards and caught all five of his targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 9-3 loss to the Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Wet and windy conditions at Soldier Field put a damper on both teams' passing games, and Swift wound up leading Chicago in receiving yards while tying Kalif Raymond for the team lead in receptions. Swift also had the Bears' longest play from scrimmage, a 32-year catch-and-run in the fourth quarter. The veteran RB has racked up 233 combined yards through two games, but Chicago's offense could look very different in Week 3 against the Eagles as Caleb Williams (hamstring) left Sunday's loss in the fourth quarter, with Tyson Bagent finishing up under center.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift - Will play Sunday
metadata.description: Swift (ankle/knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Swift and fellow RB Kyle Monangai (hamstring) were listed as limited on the Bears' first two Week 2 injury reports, but both players logged full practices Friday and thus are ready for Sunday's contest. In the Bears' 59-37 win at Carolina this past Sunday, Swift turned a 57 percent snap share into 19 touches for 134 yards from scrimmage and three rushing TDs, while Monangai handled the other 43 percent to the tune of 12 touches for 124 total yards and one TD on the ground.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Swift was limited at practice earlier in the week due to a couple of injuries that he was dealing with, but neither of them are serious and he carries no injury designation heading into the weekend. Kyle Monangai (hamstring) is also good to go, so Chicago's backfield should continue operating as usual in a divisional matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift Cleared for Week 2
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) is off the injury report and cleared for Sunday's game against Minnesota, according to Adam Schefter. Swift was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday, but neither issue will carry a game designation into Week 2. He is coming off a huge opener against Carolina, rushing 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns in Chicago's 59-37 win. Swift also caught his only target for 10 yards. The Bears gave him 19 touches despite plenty of production elsewhere in the backfield, and there is no longer an availability concern heading into Sunday's divisional matchup.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) limited again Thursday
metadata.description: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) was limited at Chicago's practice again on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran running back was limited for another practice on Thursday, as he is still managing a pair of injuries that are bothering him right now. It doesn't seem likely to affect his availability for Week 2, and fantasy managers shouldn't read much into this issue unless he goes into the weekend with an injury designation.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift - Limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Swift (ankle/knee) was limited in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Swift has been limited the last two days due to a pair of lower-body injuries to his knee and ankle. Both he and Kyle Monangai (hamstring) are on the injury report, which puts the Bears' backfield outlook in question as Sunday approaches. Friday's injury report will give firmer confirmation on Swift's status going into the Week 2 divisional matchup with the Vikings.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift Limited Again on Thursday
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (ankle, knee) was listed as a limited participant in practice on Thursday for the second straight day. Fellow backfield mate Kyle Monangai (hamstring) was also limited for a second straight day on Thursday. Chicago's backfield is uncertain for Sunday's Week 2 divisional clash against the Minnesota Vikings, but we should have a better idea of the RB picture after Friday's practice. It is possible that both Swift and Monangai practice in full on Friday and are removed from the final injury report. While Monangai had a big touchdown run in the team's Week 1 season-opening win over the Carolina Panthers, Swift handled a team-high 18 carries for 124 yards and scored three times on the ground to make a statement to begin the 2026 campaign. He added one catch on his lone target for a gain of 10 yards. If Swift is cleared to play this weekend, he will be a must-start in fantasy lineups as a low-end RB1/high-end RB2 option.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift a High-Volume Riser in Bears' Backfield
metadata.description: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift wasn't the flashiest name in fantasy drafts this year, but he continues to rise in weekly rankings after a spectacular start to the season. Swift was the fifth-highest-scoring fantasy running back in Week 1 with 18 carries, 124 rushing yards, one catch, 10 receiving yards, and a rushing touchdown. He wasn't much of a pass-catching threat, but he made an enormous impact on the ground as a key contributor to the Bears' 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers. He did cede some touches to Kyle Monangai (10 carries, 100 rushing yards, one rushing touchdown) later in the game, but all signs point to Swift remaining the primary weapon out of this backfield for the full season. It's fair to expect that the 27-year-old's ceiling may come down ever so slightly next week, assuming the Bears don't drop 59 points again. However, he's still firmly entrenched as an RB2 in fantasy football with low-end RB1 upside.

metadata.title: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) limited at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) was limited at Chicago's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Swift is a new addition to Chicago's injury report, being listed with a pair of injuries that left him limited at the team's first practice of the week. They may just be taking a cautious approach with his workload at this point, so it's worth keeping an eye on his status throughout the week, especially with backup Kyle Monangai (hamstring) also on the injury report currently.
